objects.why_kids_care: staying up until it gets dark

Every Friday morning, 10-20 words, about 15 minutes; scores like 8 out of 10 or 18 out of 20.
Friday afternoon around 2:00 PM; each kid gets 1-2 minutes; 15-25 kids in a class.
A 2-by-4 brick has 8 studs (good for arrays); towers of 10 bricks suit place value. Sold by the bucket, not singly.

objects.why_kids_care: snapping squares and triangles into castles

settings: in the block corner at school
objects.why_kids_care: building the tallest tower before it falls
objects.notes: A stacking-tower game has 54 blocks in 18 layers of 3, each block 7.5 cm long.

objects.why_kids_care: fast rounds and shouting when you win
objects.notes: A color-matching card game deck has 108 cards; rounds last 5 to 15 minutes.

objects.why_kids_care: playing go fish and war with anyone
objects.notes: A deck has 52 cards: 4 suits of 13, with 12 face cards and 4 aces. Cards 2 to 10 show their number in pips.

objects.why_kids_care: knocking over a long domino run
objects.notes: A double-six set has 28 tiles with 0 to 6 dots on each half; a double-nine set has 55. Toppling runs are measured in meters.

objects.why_kids_care: jumping three pieces in one move

Each side has 16 pieces: 8 pawns, 2 rooks, 2 knights, 2 bishops, 1 queen, 1 king. The board is 8 by 8; bishops move on diagonals.

objects.why_kids_care: waiting to see where the arrow lands
objects.notes: Spinners are split into 2 to 8 equal parts; a 4-part spinner has 90-degree sections.
Kid puzzles have 24, 48, 100, 300 or 500 pieces in rows and columns; the edge pieces form the perimeter.

objects.why_kids_care: solving it faster than a friend
objects.notes: Each face has 9 colored squares, 6 faces, 54 squares in all. Fast kids solve in under a minute; times are counted in seconds.

objects.why_kids_care: making an animal out of seven shapes
objects.notes: A set has 7 pieces: 5 triangles (2 large, 1 medium, 2 small), 1 square, 1 parallelogram. Each large triangle is 1/4 of the whole square.
Common sizes are 10 cm and 15 cm; a shelf display of 10 suits skip counting.

objects.why_kids_care: dressing them up and telling stories
objects.notes: Fashion dolls are about 29 cm tall; 18-inch dolls are 46 cm. Doll outfits cost 5 to 15 dollars.

objects.why_kids_care: lining up a whole herd by size
objects.notes: Sold singly or in tubes of 12; kids sort them by kind (meat-eater vs plant-eater) and by length.

objects.why_kids_care: building a track that loops all the way around
objects.notes: Straight pieces come in 5, 10, 15 and 20 cm; 8 curved pieces make a full circle (45 degrees each).

objects.why_kids_care: driving it around the yard from far away

objects.why_kids_care: telling it where to go and watching it obey

objects.why_kids_care: drawing a hopscotch board on the driveway
objects.notes: A bucket has 20 to 52 chunky sticks; sticks break in half. Kids draw hopscotch grids (10 squares) and measure chalk lines in feet.
Kids count tricks or how many times it goes up and down in a minute (30 to 60).
Spin times are compared in seconds (60 to 240); most have 3 arms 120 degrees apart.

objects.why_kids_care: popping every bubble then flipping it over
objects.notes: Bubbles sit in a grid, such as 5 rows of 6 (30 bubbles) or 6 rows of 6 (36); great for arrays and the last-bubble game.

objects.why_kids_care: squeezing it and watching it slowly puff back
objects.notes: Slow-rise ones take 5 to 10 seconds to puff back; kids collect them in sets.

objects.why_kids_care: building a sandcastle tower by tower
objects.notes: A pail full of wet sand makes one castle tower; a beach set with pail, shovel and 3 molds costs 5 to 15 dollars.

objects.why_kids_care: trading a pile of tickets for a prize
objects.notes: A game pays out 2 to 100 tickets a play; kids save hundreds or thousands. Tickets come out in long strips, and many arcades now store them on a card.

objects.why_kids_care: finally having enough tickets for the big one
objects.notes: Prizes cost tickets, not money: a sticker or candy 10 to 50, a small toy 100 to 500, a big plush 2,000 to 10,000.

objects.why_kids_care: grabbing a plush on the very first try
objects.notes: A kid does not own claw machines, so count_group is how many machines an arcade has. Price is for one try: 50 cents to 2 dollars, lasting about 30 seconds. A kid takes 1 to 10 tries; wins vs tries make good data problems.

objects.why_kids_care: not knowing which toy will pop out
objects.notes: Toy vending machines take quarters: 2, 4 or 8 quarters a turn; the toy comes in a plastic capsule.

objects.why_kids_care: a plane that glides across the whole room
objects.notes: Folded from one 22 by 28 cm sheet; flights are measured in meters (3 to 20 m) and seconds; folds make halves and right angles.

objects.why_kids_care: stomping hard to send it way up high
objects.notes: Stomp launchers shoot them 10 to 30 m (30 to 100 ft) high; kids compare launches in a table.

objects.why_kids_care: tossing for points at the carnival booth
objects.notes: Toss games score 1, 3 or 5 points a bag; a set has 8 bags, 4 of each color. Cornhole bags weigh 450 g; kid bags about 100 g.
Kids count jumps in a row; records go into the hundreds.

objects.why_kids_care: keeping it spinning longer than anyone
objects.notes: Spins last 10 to 90 seconds; battle tops launch with a ripcord and are timed.

objects.why_kids_care: secret messages from across the yard
objects.notes: Sold in pairs; they reach 1 to 5 km outdoors; each takes 3 AAA batteries.

objects.why_kids_care: squishing colors into snakes and cookies
objects.notes: Small tubs hold 56 g (2 oz), big tubs 140 g (5 oz); a ball of dough splits into halves and quarters.
Wooden cutting sets split an apple or pizza into 2, 3 or 4 pieces held by hook-and-loop; sets have 20 to 100 pieces.
Has 3 to 4 floors and 5 to 10 rooms; furniture packs of 5 to 10 pieces cost 10 to 20 dollars.

objects.why_kids_care: building a pyramid and knocking it down
objects.notes: Sport stacking uses 12 cups in 3-6-3 pyramids timed in seconds; toddler cups nest 8 to 10 in a row from small to big.

objects.why_kids_care: gets you in to see the animals
objects.notes: Child admission; adult tickets run $18-40. Many zoos have a family 4-pack and free kid days.

objects.why_kids_care: sharks and sea turtles up close

objects.why_kids_care: seeing the water from the boat
objects.notes: Zoo or park boat rides $5-8; paddle boat rentals $15-25 per half hour. Tour boats and paddle boats hold 10-40 people; good for how many trips a boat needs.

Wait-time signs at ride entrances (5 to 60 minutes on a normal day). count_one_kid is lines waited in one day.

objects.why_kids_care: a chance to win a prize

Child price; many museums have free days and school-group rates around $5.

objects.why_kids_care: buttons to push and things to touch

objects.why_kids_care: where the snacks get set out

objects.why_kids_care: the numbers spin fast at the pump
